subject: history
source_note: Topic structure follows the Edexcel GCSE History specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (exam boards do not publish these).

units.name: Thematic Study & Historic Environment

units.name: Modern Depth Study

connections.why: Both trace long-term change in British society, sharing the same change-and-continuity framework
Wartime injuries and conditions repeatedly drove advances in medicine
War and empire are major drivers of the migration patterns into Britain
Attitudes to migrant communities often shaped what was treated as crime and policing
The Norman conquest is a turning point in the long story of warfare and British society
Magna Carta and Angevin justice are landmarks in the development of law and punishment
Both examine medieval kingship, control and the limits of royal power
Elizabethan religious settlement is the direct legacy of the Henrician Reformation
Spanish power and the Armada are central to both the New World and Elizabethan options
Both study the expansion of European settlement and conflict across the Americas
Cold War superpower rivalry shaped conflict in the Middle East
Understanding the Soviet state illuminates one side of the Cold War
US Cold War foreign policy is the backdrop to the conflict in Vietnam
Both examine how a fragile state gave way to a twentieth-century dictatorship
Both analyse how a totalitarian regime built and maintained control
Both study the building of a communist one-party state and its consequences
Civil-rights struggles in the USA echo the themes of belonging and discrimination
